claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Calcinotto et al., 2019

claims.claim: The mechanisms underlying therapy-induced senescence are usually connected to the DNA damage response.
claims.source: The mechanisms underlying TIS are usually connected to the DDR.
claims.evidence: Stated as established knowledge

claims.claim: Palbociclib, Doxorubicin, Bleomycin, Docetaxel, Cyclophosphamide, Etoposide, Vincristine, and Cisplatin are therapy-induced senescence drugs used for human cancer treatment.
claims.source: Presently, several TIS drugs are used for human cancer treatment, including Palbociclib, Doxorubicin, Bleomycin, Docetaxel, Cyclophosphamide, Etoposide, Vincristine, and Cisplatin (Ewald et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Ewald et al., 2010

claims.claim: Palbociclib is currently considered the most relevant prosenescent compound in the clinic.
claims.source: Among all of them, the CDK4/6 inhibitor Palbociclib is currently considered the most relevant prosenescent compound in the clinic.
claims.evidence: Stated as current clinical knowledge

claims.claim: The accumulation of senescent cells after therapy-induced senescence has been shown to promote tumour relapse with increased malignancy.
claims.source: Indeed, the accumulation of SCs after TIS has been shown to promote tumour relapse with increased malignancy and premature aging features in human adults and children after chemotherapy (Marcoux et al., 2013; Ness et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Marcoux et al., 2013 and Ness et al., 2015

claims.claim: After therapy-induced senescence, some senescent tumour cells are able to escape from cell cycle blockade and acquire stemness properties with highly aggressive growth potential.
claims.source: Furthermore, a recent study has demonstrated that, after TIS, some senescent tumour cells are able to escape from cell cycle blockade and acquire stemness properties with highly aggressive growth potential, which contradicts the terminal proliferative phenotype and has profound implications for the treatment outcome (Milanovic et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Milanovic et al., 2018

claims.claim: Current therapeutic strategies for cancer generally encompass a double approach involving an initial pro-senescent step followed by an anti-senescent phase.
claims.source: As a result, current therapeutic strategies generally encompass a double approach, involving an initial pro-senescent step followed by an anti-senescent phase (Calcinotto et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Calcinotto et al., 2019

claims.claim: Senescent cells have been found during development of mouse and human embryos.
claims.source: So far, SCs have been found during development of mouse and human embryos (Chuprin et al., 2013; Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013), but also in naked mole rats (Zhao et al., 2018), birds (Gibaja et al., 2019; Nacher et al., 2006; Storer et al., 2013), amphibians (Davaapil et al., 2017; Villiard et al., 2017), and fish (Da Silva-Álvarez et al., 2020; Villiard et al., 2017) embryos and/or larvae.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Chuprin et al., 2013; Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013

claims.claim: Senescent cells have been found in naked mole rat embryos.
claims.source: So far, SCs have been found during development of mouse and human embryos (Chuprin et al., 2013; Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013), but also in naked mole rats (Zhao et al., 2018), birds (Gibaja et al., 2019; Nacher et al., 2006; Storer et al., 2013), amphibians (Davaapil et al., 2017; Villiard et al., 2017), and fish (Da Silva-Álvarez et al., 2020; Villiard et al., 2017) embryos and/or larvae.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2018

claims.claim: Senescent cells have been found in bird embryos and/or larvae.
claims.source: So far, SCs have been found during development of mouse and human embryos (Chuprin et al., 2013; Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013), but also in naked mole rats (Zhao et al., 2018), birds (Gibaja et al., 2019; Nacher et al., 2006; Storer et al., 2013), amphibians (Davaapil et al., 2017; Villiard et al., 2017), and fish (Da Silva-Álvarez et al., 2020; Villiard et al., 2017) embryos and/or larvae.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Gibaja et al., 2019; Nacher et al., 2006; Storer et al., 2013

claims.claim: Senescent cells have been found in amphibian embryos and/or larvae.
claims.source: So far, SCs have been found during development of mouse and human embryos (Chuprin et al., 2013; Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013), but also in naked mole rats (Zhao et al., 2018), birds (Gibaja et al., 2019; Nacher et al., 2006; Storer et al., 2013), amphibians (Davaapil et al., 2017; Villiard et al., 2017), and fish (Da Silva-Álvarez et al., 2020; Villiard et al., 2017) embryos and/or larvae.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Davaapil et al., 2017 and Villiard et al., 2017

claims.claim: Senescent cells have been found in fish embryos and/or larvae.
claims.source: So far, SCs have been found during development of mouse and human embryos (Chuprin et al., 2013; Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013), but also in naked mole rats (Zhao et al., 2018), birds (Gibaja et al., 2019; Nacher et al., 2006; Storer et al., 2013), amphibians (Davaapil et al., 2017; Villiard et al., 2017), and fish (Da Silva-Álvarez et al., 2020; Villiard et al., 2017) embryos and/or larvae.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Da Silva-Álvarez et al., 2020 and Villiard et al., 2017

claims.claim: Senescent cells in developing embryonic structures exhibit SA-β-gal activity and upregulation of p21CIP1, while expression of p53, p16INK4a, and DNA damage response is absent.
claims.source: SCs in developing embryonic structures exhibit SA-β-gal activity and upregulation of p21CIP1, while expression of other senescence markers, like p53, p16INK4a, and DDR, is absent (Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013

claims.claim: Genetic disruption of p21CIP1 or senolytic treatment results in loss of senescence and patterning abnormalities in various structures during development.
claims.source: Indeed, genetic disruption of p21CIP1 or senolytic treatment results in loss of senescence and patterning abnormalities in various structures (Davaapil et al., 2017; Gibaja et al., 2019; Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Davaapil et al., 2017; Gibaja et al., 2019; Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013

claims.claim: Patterning defects during development are only observed transiently and are eventually compensated by other mechanisms, namely apoptosis.
claims.source: Interestingly, patterning defects are only observed transiently and are eventually compensated by other mechanisms, namely apoptosis (Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013; Storer et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Muñoz-Espín et al., 2013 and Storer et al., 2013

claims.claim: Senescent cells are intrinsic to development but not essential.
claims.source: This suggests that SCs are intrinsic to development but not essential.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the observation that patterning defects are compensated

claims.claim: Developmental senescence is a highly organized and programmed process with precise patterns in time and space.
claims.source: Overall, existing studies suggest that developmental senescence is not a damage-triggered event but rather a highly organized and programmed process with precise patterns in time and space, which may be orchestrated by other cues such as biophysical forces during morphogenesis.
claims.evidence: Inferred from developmental studies

claims.claim: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in the liver.
claims.source: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in several organs, such as the liver (Krizhanovsky et al., 2008), the skin (Demaria et al., 2014; Jun and Lau, 2010), the heart (Meyer et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2013), and the lung (Schafer et al., 2017; Table 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Krizhanovsky et al., 2008

claims.claim: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in the skin.
claims.source: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in several organs, such as the liver (Krizhanovsky et al., 2008), the skin (Demaria et al., 2014; Jun and Lau, 2010), the heart (Meyer et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2013), and the lung (Schafer et al., 2017; Table 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Demaria et al., 2014 and Jun and Lau, 2010

claims.claim: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in the heart.
claims.source: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in several organs, such as the liver (Krizhanovsky et al., 2008), the skin (Demaria et al., 2014; Jun and Lau, 2010), the heart (Meyer et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2013), and the lung (Schafer et al., 2017; Table 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Meyer et al., 2016 and Zhu et al., 2013

claims.claim: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in the lung.
claims.source: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in several organs, such as the liver (Krizhanovsky et al., 2008), the skin (Demaria et al., 2014; Jun and Lau, 2010), the heart (Meyer et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2013), and the lung (Schafer et al., 2017; Table 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Schafer et al., 2017

claims.claim: Senescent cells are closely associated with the levels of fibrotic tissue generated upon wound resolution.
claims.source: In all cases, SCs seem to be closely associated with the levels of fibrotic tissue generated upon wound resolution, which in turn affect the outcome of the repair process (Baker et al., 2016; Yun, 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Baker et al., 2016 and Yun, 2018

claims.claim: CCN1 elicits a senescence response in fibroblasts by triggering p53 and p16INK4a via ERK and p38MAPK pathways in the skin.
claims.source: In the skin, CCN1, a matricellular protein expressed upon wound healing, elicits a senescence response in fibroblasts by triggering p53 and p16INK4a via ERK and p38MAPK pathways (Jun and Lau, 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Jun and Lau, 2010

claims.claim: CCN1-induced senescence response controls the proliferation of fibroblasts and ECM deposition, limiting the fibrotic scar and contributing to the healing process.
claims.source: This response controls the proliferation of fibroblasts and ECM deposition, limiting the fibrotic scar and contributing to the healing process.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of CCN1 function

claims.claim: Defects in CCN1 lead to fibrosis exacerbation.
claims.source: Importantly, defects in CCN1 lead to fibrosis exacerbation (Jun and Lau, 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Jun and Lau, 2010

claims.claim: A transient accumulation of senescent fibroblasts and endothelial cells at the wound site induces myofibroblast differentiation through secretion of PDGF-AA.
claims.source: Also in the skin, in a more recent study using the p16-3MR transgenic model, Demaria and colleagues demonstrated that a transient accumulation of senescent fibroblasts and endothelial cells at the wound site induces myofibroblast differentiation through secretion of platelet growth factor AA (PDGF-AA) (Demaria et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Demaria et al., 2014

claims.claim: Elimination of p16+ cells results in delayed wound healing and increased fibrosis.
claims.source: Elimination of p16+ cells resulted in delayed wound healing and increased fibrosis.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result

claims.claim: Topical administration of PDGF-AA reverts the delay in wound closure while maintaining the levels of fibrotic tissue.
claims.source: Notably, topical administration of PDGF-AA reverted the delay in wound closure while maintaining the levels of fibrotic tissue, suggesting more SASP factors (likely MMPs) are involved in the healing process.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result with inference about MMPs

claims.claim: Administration of CCl4 induces fibrotic scarring and senescence in hepatic stellate cells via a CCN1/p53/p16INK4a pathway in a mouse model of chronic liver damage.
claims.source: In a mouse model of chronic liver damage, the administration of CCl4 induces fibrotic scarring and senescence in hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) also via a CCN1/p53/p16INK4a pathway (Krizhanovsky et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Krizhanovsky et al., 2008

claims.claim: Senescent hepatic stellate cells facilitate fibrotic resolution through secretion of MMPs.
claims.source: Senescent HSCs facilitate fibrotic resolution through secretion of MMPs.
claims.evidence: Stated as established finding

claims.claim: Senescent hepatic stellate cells recruit NK cells to promote their own elimination.
claims.source: Finally, the cycle is completed by recruitment of NK cells to promote their own elimination.
claims.evidence: Stated as part of the senescence cycle in liver

claims.claim: p53;INK4A/ARF null mice display decreased numbers of senescent hepatic stellate cells and extensive cirrhosis upon CCl4 treatment.
claims.source: Moreover, p53;INK4A/ARF null mice displayed decreased numbers of senescent HSCs and extensive cirrhosis upon CCl4 treatment (Krizhanovsky et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Krizhanovsky et al., 2008

claims.claim: The SASP of senescent endothelial cells stimulates neutrophil recruitment and the extrusion of neutrophil extracellular traps, which remove dysfunctional endothelial senescent cells and facilitate vascular pruning and repair in ischemic retinopathy.
claims.source: In a recent study using both human and mouse models of ischemic retinopathy, the SASP of senescent endothelial cells stimulated neutrophil recruitment and the extrusion of neutrophil extracellular traps, which both removed dysfunctional endothelial SCs and facilitated vascular pruning and repair (Binet et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Binet et al., 2020

claims.claim: Cardiac myofibroblasts enter senescence through a CCN1-dependent manner in mouse models of cardiac hypertrophy and heart infarction, reducing fibrosis in the short-term and improving heart function.
claims.source: In mouse models of cardiac hypertrophy and heart infarction, cardiac myofibroblasts enter senescence through a CCN1-dependent manner, reducing fibrosis in the short-term and improving heart function (Meyer et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Meyer et al., 2016 and Zhu et al., 2013

claims.claim: After cardiac ischaemia-reperfusion injury, a long-term oxidative stress-induced senescence response in cardiomyocytes and interstitial cells promotes fibrosis and mediates a pro-inflammatory SASP, impairing heart function.
claims.source: However, after cardiac ischaemia-reperfusion injury, a long-term oxidative stress-induced senescence response in cardiomyocytes and interstitial cells promotes fibrosis and mediates a pro-inflammatory SASP, impairing heart function (Dookun et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Dookun et al., 2020

claims.claim: In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, senescent epithelial cells and fibroblasts accumulate continuously over time, inducing myofibroblast differentiation and exacerbating the fibrotic response.
claims.source: Similarly, in a mouse model of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a chronic lung disease characterized by decreased lung function due to persistent scarring, senescent epithelial cells and fibroblasts accumulate continuously over time, inducing myofibroblast differentiation and exacerbating the fibrotic response (Schafer et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Schafer et al., 2017

claims.claim: Elimination of senescent cells improves the disease condition in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
claims.source: In this case, the elimination of SCs improves the disease condition.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result in IPF context

claims.claim: Timely and coordinated activation of senescent cells controls the early fibrotic response and is beneficial for wound repair.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that timely and coordinated activation of SCs controls the early fibrotic response and is beneficial for wound repair.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the collective evidence on wound healing

claims.claim: In the absence of proper clearance, persistent senescent cells accumulate and have a negative impact in tissue repair.
claims.source: Yet, in the absence of proper clearance, persistent SCs accumulate and have a negative impact in tissue repair (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: Inferred from the collective evidence with reference to Figure 2

claims.claim: A recurrent turnover of senescence occurs during limb regeneration in the salamander.
claims.source: In 2015, the team of Jeremy Brockes (UCL, London) reported a recurrent turnover of senescence during limb regeneration in the salamander (Yun et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Yun et al., 2015

claims.claim: Senescent cells are transiently induced near the amputation plane throughout regeneration in salamander limbs and subsequently cleared by a macrophage-dependent immunosurveillance mechanism.
claims.source: SCs were transiently induced near the amputation plane throughout regeneration and subsequently cleared by a macrophage-dependent immunosurveillance mechanism.
claims.evidence: Stated as finding from salamander study

claims.claim: A transient burst of SA-β-gal+ cardiac fibroblasts was reported in zebrafish and neonatal mouse hearts after an injury.
claims.source: In 2019, a transient burst of SA-β-gal+ cardiac fibroblasts was reported in zebrafish and neonatal mouse hearts after an injury (Sarig et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Sarig et al., 2019

claims.claim: Telomerase-deficient zebrafish display an aberrant accumulation of senescent cells and fail to regenerate their hearts.
claims.source: Even though the effects of senescence on cardiac regeneration are yet to be determined, a study from 2015 demonstrated that telomerase-deficient zebrafish display an aberrant accumulation of SCs and fail to regenerate their hearts (Bednarek et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Bednarek et al., 2015

claims.claim: A transient accumulation of senescent cells occurs after zebrafish caudal fin amputation.
claims.source: Also in 2019, another study showed evidence of a transient accumulation of SCs after zebrafish caudal fin amputation (Da Silva‐Álvarez et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Da Silva‐Álvarez et al., 2019

claims.claim: Tissue regeneration is impaired by removal of senescent cells with a senolytic drug in zebrafish caudal fin.
claims.source: In this case, tissue regeneration was impaired by removal of SCs with a senolytic drug, a type of drug that acts by inducing apoptosis in SCs (Zhu et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2015

claims.claim: Senescence of fibro-adipogenic progenitors in response to exercise-induced muscle damage is necessary to promote functional recovery and muscle regeneration in a mouse model of chronic inflammatory myopathy.
claims.source: In a mouse model of chronic inflammatory myopathy, senescence of fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) in response to exercise-induced muscle damage is necessary to promote functional recovery and muscle regeneration (Saito et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Saito et al., 2020

claims.claim: The expression of p53 is upregulated in the rat soleus muscle after a spinal cord injury.
claims.source: In addition, the expression of p53 was found to be upregulated in the rat soleus muscle after a spinal cord injury (Graham et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Graham et al., 2020

claims.claim: TGF-β secretion-mediated paracrine senescence of cholangiocytes and hepatocytes has deleterious repercussions in the surrounding microenvironment and impairs liver regeneration in a mouse model of biliary injury.
claims.source: In a mouse model of biliary injury, TGF-β secretion-mediated paracrine senescence of cholangiocytes and hepatocytes was shown to have deleterious repercussions in the surrounding microenvironment and impair liver regeneration (Ferreira-Gonzalez et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Ferreira-Gonzalez et al., 2018

claims.claim: Inhibition of TGF-β signalling disrupts the continuous propagation of senescence, reduces collagen deposition, and restores liver function in biliary injury.
claims.source: The inhibition of TGF-β signalling disrupted the continuous propagation of senescence, reduced collagen deposition, and restored liver function.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result

claims.claim: The regenerating zebrafish exhibits a transient accumulation of senescent cells at the lesion periphery after spinal cord injury, which are then cleared out.
claims.source: In this study, the regenerating zebrafish exhibits a transient accumulation of SCs at the lesion periphery, which are then cleared out.
claims.evidence: Stated as finding from the study

claims.claim: In injured mice, senescent cells persistently accumulate over time after spinal cord injury and are not eliminated.
claims.source: In contrast, in the injured mice SCs persistently accumulate over time and are not eliminated.
claims.evidence: Stated as finding from the study

claims.claim: Targeting of senescent cells in the mouse spinal cord to prevent their accumulation after injury results in improved motor, sensory, and bladder functions.
claims.source: Targeting of SCs in the mouse spinal cord in order to prevent their accumulation after injury resulted in improved motor, sensory, and bladder functions, supported by beneficial effects on myelin preservation, axonal growth, fibrotic resolution, and inflammation.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result

claims.claim: Targeting of senescent cells in the mouse spinal cord after injury is accompanied by a reduced secretion of pro-fibrotic and pro-inflammatory factors in the injury microenvironment.
claims.source: These effects were accompanied by a reduced secretion of pro-fibrotic and pro-inflammatory factors in the injury microenvironment (Table 1).
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result with reference to Table 1

claims.claim: Expression of the four Yamanaka factors activates senescence markers in targeting cells in vitro.
claims.source: In vitro, the expression of the four Yamanaka factors (OCT3/4, SOX2, KLF4 and c-MYC, OSKM) activates senescence markers in targeting cells, such as SA-β-gal, p16INK4a, p21CIP1, and SAHF (Banito et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Banito et al., 2009

claims.claim: The iPS cell generation efficiency is approximately 0.02%.
claims.source: This seemingly intrinsic barrier to reprogramming probably explains why the iPS cell generation efficiency is so low (≈0.02%) (Takahashi et al., 2007; Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Takahashi et al., 2007 and Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006

claims.claim: Silencing of senescence-associated genes like p53, CIP1, and INK4a increases iPS cell generation rate from mouse and human fibroblasts.
claims.source: In fact, silencing of senescence-associated genes like p53, CIP1, and INK4a has been shown to increase iPS cell generation rate from mouse and human fibroblasts (Banito et al., 2009; Hong et al., 2009; Li et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Banito et al., 2009; Hong et al., 2009; Li et al., 2009

claims.claim: i4F wild-type mice exhibit co-expression of SA-β-gal and NANOG.
claims.source: i4F wild-type mice exhibited co-expression of SA-β-gal and NANOG, a pluripotency marker (Mosteiro et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Mosteiro et al., 2016

claims.claim: Without INK4a/ARF, co-expression of SA-β-gal and NANOG is lost in i4F mice.
claims.source: Without INK4a/ARF, this co-expression was lost.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result

claims.claim: In mouse models of lung and muscle damage in which senescence is induced at the lesion sites, the efficiency of reprogramming of i4F mice is increased.
claims.source: Remarkably, in mouse models of lung and muscle damage in which senescence is induced at the lesion sites, the efficiency of reprogramming of i4F mice was increased (Chiche et al., 2017; Mosteiro et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Chiche et al., 2017 and Mosteiro et al., 2016

claims.claim: Reprogramming efficiency is enhanced in conditions that elicit senescence activation, including Palbociclib treatment, irradiation, and aging.
claims.source: This efficiency was also enhanced in conditions that elicit senescence activation, including Palbociclib treatment, irradiation, and even aging.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental finding

claims.claim: Reprogramming is decreased after p16INK4a deletion or treatment with the senolytic drug ABT-263.
claims.source: On the other hand, reprogramming was decreased after p16INK4a deletion or treatment with the senolytic drug ABT-263 (Chiche et al., 2017; Mosteiro et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Chiche et al., 2017 and Mosteiro et al., 2016

claims.claim: Senescence-induced favourable environment for reprogramming is mediated by secretion of IL-6 that activates the JAK/STAT target PIM1 to promote cellular plasticity.
claims.source: This senescence-induced favourable environment for reprogramming was found to be mediated by secretion of the SASP factor IL-6 that activates the JAK/STAT target PIM1 to promote cellular plasticity, which can be reverted by treatment with IL-6 antibodies (Chiche et al., 2017; Mosteiro et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Chiche et al., 2017 and Mosteiro et al., 2016

claims.claim: Ras-mediated oncogene-induced senescence in the skin and liver induces the expression of stemness markers such as CD34, Lgr6, and Nestin in senescent keratinocytes.
claims.source: In another study, Ras-mediated OIS in the skin and liver was shown to induce the expression of stemness markers, such as CD34, Lgr6, and Nestin, in senescent keratinocytes (Ritschka et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Ritschka et al., 2017

claims.claim: Expression of stemness markers in senescent keratinocytes is SASP-dependent and is abolished with NF-κB inhibition.
claims.source: This was also demonstrated to be SASP-dependent, as it was abolished with nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) inhibition.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result

claims.claim: Expression of stemness markers is overcome by senescence features upon a longer (6 days) exposure to the OIS-driven SASP.
claims.source: However, the expression of stemness markers was overcome by senescence features upon a longer (6 days) exposure to the OIS-driven SASP, which was proposed as a cell-intrinsic anti-tumourigenic response to counteract stemness.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result with interpretation

claims.claim: Senescent liver sinusoid endothelial cells have important structural and functional roles in the aging organism and cannot be replaced after removal.
claims.source: In fact, a recent study has proven that senescent liver sinusoid endothelial cells have important structural and functional roles in the aging organism and cannot be replaced after removal (Grosse et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Grosse et al., 2020

claims.claim: Acute elimination of senescent liver sinusoid endothelial cells promotes liver and perivascular tissue fibrosis, as well as health deterioration.
claims.source: Consequently, their acute elimination promoted liver and perivascular tissue fibrosis, as well as health deterioration.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result

claims.claim: Transcriptomic analysis revealed the upregulation of pro-survival genes in senescent cells, namely those involving the anti-apoptotic PI3K/AKT pathway and BCL-2 family proteins.
claims.source: Transcriptomic analysis revealed the upregulation of pro-survival genes in SCs, namely those involving the anti-apoptotic PI3K/AKT pathway and BCL-2 family proteins, as compared to normal cells (Zhu et al., 2015), and identified drugs that can counteract the pro-survival genes and cause apoptosis.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2015

claims.claim: Senolytic agents such as Dasatinib, Quercetin, and Navitoclax are being tested in several clinical trials for the treatment of senescence/age-associated disorders and cancer.
claims.source: Senolytic agents such as Dasatinib, Quercetin, and Navitoclax (also known as ABT-263) are being tested in several clinical trials for the treatment of specific types of senescence/age-associated disorders and cancer (Paez-Ribes et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Paez-Ribes et al., 2019

claims.claim: In vitro studies have reported evidence for NK and CD4+ T cell sensitization towards certain types of senescent cells upon administration of anti-DPP4 and anti-Vimentin antibodies, respectively.
claims.source: In vitro studies have reported evidence for NK and CD4+ T cell sensitization towards certain types of SCs upon administration of anti-DPP4 (a surface peptidase) and anti-Vimentin (membrane-bound protein) antibodies, respectively (Frescas et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Frescas et al., 2017 and Kim et al., 2017

claims.claim: Chimeric antigen receptor T cells that target urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor have senolytic potential.
claims.source: Recently, a ground-breaking study reported the senolytic potential of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells that target urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR), a cell-surface protein that was found to be broadly expressed during senescence (Figure 1; Amor et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Amor et al., 2020 and reference to Figure 1

claims.claim: uPAR-specific CAR T cells efficiently eliminate senescent cells in different in vitro and in vivo contexts.
claims.source: uPAR-specific CAR T cells were shown to efficiently eliminate SCs in different in vitro and in vivo contexts, unveiling a promising therapeutic strategy for senescence-associated pathologies.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result

claims.claim: CD9 is upregulated in endothelial cells and is associated with atherosclerotic plaque formation.
claims.source: For example, a recent study has established an association between the upregulation of CD9 (a membrane protein known to regulate cell adhesion and migration) in endothelial cells and atherosclerotic plaque formation (Cho et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Cho et al., 2020

claims.claim: CD9 regulates cellular senescence through a phosphatidylinositide 3 kinase-AKT-mTOR-p53 signalling pathway.
claims.source: CD9 regulated cellular senescence through a phosphatidylinositide 3 kinase-AKT-mTOR-p53 signalling pathway and its expression increased in arterial tissues with age, contributing to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental finding

claims.claim: CD9 expression increases in arterial tissues with age, contributing to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
claims.source: CD9 regulated cellular senescence through a phosphatidylinositide 3 kinase-AKT-mTOR-p53 signalling pathway and its expression increased in arterial tissues with age, contributing to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental finding

claims.claim: A combination of 5‐Azacytydine and Resveratrol reverses the senescent phenotype of adipose stem cells through modulation of mitochondrial dynamics and autophagy.
claims.source: In 2018, Kornicka and colleagues demonstrated that a combination of 5‐Azacytydine and Resveratrol reversed the senescent phenotype of adipose stem cells through modulation of mitochondrial dynamics and autophagy (Kornicka et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Kornicka et al., 2019

claims.claim: Upon combinatorial treatment with 5‐Azacytydine and Resveratrol, adipose stem cells exhibit increased proliferation rate, decreased SA-β-gal activity, and lower reactive oxygen species accumulation.
claims.source: Upon this combinatorial treatment, adipose stem cells exhibited increased proliferation rate, decreased SA-β-gal activity, and lower reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation.
claims.evidence: Stated as experimental result

claims.claim: Replicative senescent retinal pigment epithelial cells co-cultured with embryonic stem cells display increased proliferative capacity re-entering the S and G2/M cycle phases.
claims.source: Similar results were found in replicative senescent retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells co-cultured with embryonic stem cells (Wang et al., 2020). In this case, senescent RPE cells displayed increased proliferative capacity re-entering the S and G2/M cycle phases, along with the downregulation of several senescence biomarkers, such as SA-β-gal, p53, p21CIP1, p16INK4a.

claims.claim: 3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 inhibition suppresses NF-κB and mTOR signalling and abolishes senescence hallmarks in senescent human dermal fibroblasts, restoring their quiescent state.
claims.source: Though the mechanisms by which the senescent state can be reverted are still unclear, it has been shown that 3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 (PDK1) inhibition suppresses NF-κB and mTOR signalling and abolishes senescence hallmarks in senescent human dermal fibroblasts, restoring their quiescent state (An et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to An et al., 2020

claims.claim: The senescence programme entails deep epigenetic alterations which permit a tight regulation of transcriptional activities essential to its timely execution.
claims.source: Importantly, the senescence programme entails deep epigenetic alterations which permit a tight regulation of transcriptional activities that is essential to its timely execution.
claims.evidence: Stated as established knowledge

claims.claim: The epigenetic network of senescence is orchestrated by activator protein 1, who 'imprints' the senescence enhancer landscape that drives the transcriptional programme of senescent cells and determines their fate.
claims.source: This network was found to be orchestrated by activator protein 1 (AP-1), who 'imprints' the senescence enhancer landscape that drives the transcriptional programme of SCs and determines their fate (Martínez-Zamudio et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Martínez-Zamudio et al., 2020

claims.claim: The balance between senescence and apoptosis upon genotoxic stress is regulated by high mobility group box‐1 proteins.
claims.source: It has been suggested that the balance between senescence and apoptosis upon genotoxic stress is regulated by high mobility group box‐1 (HMGB1) proteins (Lee et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2019

claims.claim: A crosstalk between the telomere shortening/p53 and AKT/FoxO signalling pathways regulates an apoptosis-to-senescence switch during aging.
claims.source: In addition, a crosstalk between the telomere shortening/p53 and AKT/FoxO signalling pathways has been proposed to regulate an apoptosis-to-senescence switch during aging (El Maï et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to El Maï et al., 2020

claims.claim: Organs of regenerating animals such as the zebrafish often display senescence features during their developmental stages.
claims.source: In fact, organs of regenerating animals, such as the zebrafish, often display senescence features during their developmental stages (Da Silva-Álvarez et al., 2020), suggesting a link between regeneration and the recapitulation of developmental senescence.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Da Silva-Álvarez et al., 2020

claims.claim: Two distinct populations of p16INK4a+ and p21CIP1+ senescent cells respectively promote and impair the regenerative capacity of the mouse liver.
claims.source: This may be further complicated by the existence of different SC populations within the same context, as was recently demonstrated in the mouse liver where two distinct populations of p16INK4a+ and p21CIP1+ SCs have been shown to respectively promote and impair the regenerative capacity of the organ (Ritschka et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Ritschka et al., 2020

claims.claim: The beneficial roles of senescence all share a transient profile.
claims.source: While the beneficial roles of senescence all share a transient profile, the deleterious functions of SCs are associated to their lingering persistence, namely the chronic exposure to their SASP (Figure 2; Rhinn et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Inferred from the collective evidence with reference to Figure 2 and citation to Rhinn et al., 2019

claims.claim: The deleterious functions of senescent cells are associated to their lingering persistence and chronic exposure to their SASP.
claims.source: While the beneficial roles of senescence all share a transient profile, the deleterious functions of SCs are associated to their lingering persistence, namely the chronic exposure to their SASP (Figure 2; Rhinn et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Inferred from the collective evidence with reference to Figure 2 and citation to Rhinn et al., 2019

results.result: Cellular senescence was historically characterized as replicative senescence, where normal diploid cells in culture undergo limited divisions, enter permanent cell cycle arrest, remain viable for weeks, and this proliferation limit is attributed to progressive telomere shortening. This phenomenon accumulates in an age-dependent manner in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C4 are well-supported by citations to foundational work (Hayflick and Moorhead 1961, Hayflick 1965, Harley et al. 1990, Dimri et al. 1995). These claims establish the historical discovery and characterization of replicative senescence, forming the basis for understanding cellular senescence as a biological phenomenon. The evidence is consistent and builds logically from initial observations to molecular mechanisms.

results.result: Cellular senescence can be induced by diverse stress signals beyond telomere erosion, including oncogene activation (oncogene-induced senescence), oxidative stress, chemotherapy, iPS cell reprogramming, irradiation, and cytokine treatment. This demonstrates that senescence and aging are not synonymous, and senescent cells can be triggered independently of organismal age.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C13 are supported by multiple citations (Serrano et al. 1997, Chen et al. 1995, Schmitt et al. 2002, Krizhanovsky and Lowe 2009, Le et al. 2010, Braumüller et al. 2013, Rodier and Campisi 2011). The evidence establishes that senescence is a stress response program that can be triggered by various stimuli, not just aging. This is a fundamental conceptual advance in the field, distinguishing senescence as a cellular state from organismal aging.

results.result: Senescent cells undergo numerous phenotypic changes, remain metabolically active with a complex secretory phenotype (SASP), and have emerged as beneficial players in physiological processes including embryonic development, cellular reprogramming, wound healing, and tissue repair.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C18 are supported by citations (Muñoz-Espín and Serrano 2014, Rhinn et al. 2019) and reference to Figure 1. These claims establish the modern understanding of senescent cells as active participants in physiological processes rather than merely dysfunctional cells. The evidence demonstrates a paradigm shift in how senescence is conceptualized.

results.result: No single biomarker is absolutely specific for senescence. Common markers like cell cycle arrest (pRB, p53), p16INK4a, p21CIP1, SA-β-gal, DNA-SCARS, SAHF, lipid profiles, and mitochondrial dysfunction all show context-dependent expression and can be present in non-senescent cells or absent in some senescent cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C31 are well-supported by multiple citations (Rodier and Campisi 2011, Hernandez-Segura et al. 2017, Sharpless and Sherr 2015, Huang and Rivera-Pérez 2014, Xu et al. 2019, Lee et al. 2006, Hall et al. 2017, Di Micco et al. 2011, Kennedy et al. 2010, Rodier et al. 2011, Eisner et al. 2018, Quijano et al. 2012). This comprehensive assessment of biomarker limitations is critical for proper experimental design and interpretation. The evidence clearly demonstrates the heterogeneity of senescence and the need for multi-parametric approaches.

results.result: Terminally differentiated cells, including post-mitotic neurons, can develop a senescent phenotype. This has been observed in cortical neurons in aging rodent and human brains, and neurons can be induced to senesce after spinal cord injury.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C34 are supported by multiple citations (Chinta et al. 2015, Jurk et al. 2012, Kang et al. 2015, Moreno-Blas et al. 2019, Walton and Andersen 2019, Paramos-de-Carvalho et al. 2021). This extends the concept of senescence beyond proliferating cells to post-mitotic cells, which is an important conceptual advance. The evidence is consistent across multiple studies and species.

results.result: The senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) comprises growth factors, chemokines, cytokines, extracellular matrix components, and proteases. Through the SASP, senescent cells modulate the surrounding environment and exert pathophysiological effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C37 are supported by citations (Krtolica et al. 2001, Le et al. 2010) and reference to Figure 1. The SASP is established as a central feature of senescence that mediates both beneficial and detrimental effects. The evidence clearly demonstrates the complexity and importance of the SASP in senescence biology.

results.result: Cellular senescence has been implicated in a wide range of biological activities including aging, tumor progression, tumor suppression, development, wound healing, and regeneration.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C43 are supported by citations (Rhinn et al. 2019, Rodier and Campisi 2011). These claims establish the broad biological relevance of senescence across multiple contexts. The evidence demonstrates that senescence is not a single phenomenon but participates in diverse biological processes.

results.result: Continuous exposure to the SASP induces paracrine senescence in bystander normal cells both in vitro and in vivo. This paracrine senescence mediates deleterious effects on tissue homeostasis, promoting tumourigenesis, aging-related organ dysfunction, and impairing regeneration.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C47 are supported by citations (Acosta et al. 2013, Nelson et al. 2012, Campisi 2005, Ferreira-Gonzalez et al. 2018, Gonzalez-Meljem et al. 2018). The concept of paracrine senescence is important for understanding how senescent cells can have systemic effects. The evidence demonstrates that SASP-mediated propagation of senescence is a key mechanism of pathology.

results.result: Some SASP factors such as CSF1, CCL2, and IL-8 recruit the immune system to promote self-clearance of senescent cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C48 is supported by citation (Muñoz-Espín and Serrano 2014). This demonstrates that the SASP can have self-limiting effects through immune recruitment, which is important for understanding senescence dynamics and potential therapeutic approaches.

results.result: The manifestation of each senescence hallmark is context-dependent and varies according to the stress trigger, cell or tissue type, and time from induction. Therefore, a multi-parametric approach is required to define a senescence signature.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C50 are supported by citation (Calcinotto et al. 2019) and inference from the discussion of senescence heterogeneity. This establishes the methodological requirement for comprehensive characterization of senescence. The evidence clearly demonstrates the complexity and context-dependence of senescence.

results.result: Recent advances include a proteomic atlas of SASP factors from senescent fibroblasts and epithelial cells, and a three-step multi-marker system for identifying senescent cells with improved accuracy.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C52 are supported by citations (Basisty et al. 2020, Gorgoulis et al. 2019). These represent methodological advances that address the challenge of senescence heterogeneity and biomarker specificity. The evidence demonstrates progress in developing more rigorous approaches to senescence identification.

results.result: Senescent cells are found in many tissues throughout life in zebrafish, rodents, primates, and humans. Though relatively rare in young organisms, they accumulate with age in several organs including skin, heart, lung, spleen, kidney, and liver.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C54 are supported by citations (Campisi 2005, Dimri et al. 1995, Jeyapalan et al. 2007, Kishi 2004, Wang et al. 2009, Yang and Fogo 2010). This establishes the in vivo relevance of senescence across species and tissues, and the age-dependent accumulation pattern. The evidence is consistent across multiple studies and species.

results.result: Senescence has been associated with a wide range of human age-associated pathologies including cancer, fibrosis, cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes, obesity, sarcopenia, osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, and neurological disorders.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C63 are supported by citations (Calcinotto et al. 2019, van Deursen 2014). This establishes the clinical relevance of senescence across multiple disease contexts. The evidence demonstrates the broad pathological impact of senescent cell accumulation.

results.result: Ablation of p16INK4a+ cells improves many age-related disease symptoms in progeroid mouse models, reinforcing a detrimental role of senescent cells in aged tissues.
results.evaluation: Claim C64 is supported by citations (Baker et al. 2011, Rhinn et al. 2019). This provides direct experimental evidence that senescent cells contribute to age-related pathology. The use of genetic ablation models provides strong causal evidence.

results.result: Senescence plays a role in the decline of regenerative capacity with aging by functionally depleting stem cell progenitor pools. In aged muscle, geriatric muscle stem cells undergo a quiescence-senescence switch triggered by increased p38MAPK activation and p16INK4a expression, and inhibition of these pathways restores regenerative function.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C67 are supported by citations (Braun et al. 2012, Janzen et al. 2006, Cosgrove et al. 2014, Sousa-Victor et al. 2014). This demonstrates a specific mechanism by which senescence impairs regeneration through stem cell dysfunction. The evidence includes both observational and interventional studies.

results.result: In the aging heart, cardiac progenitor cells progressively lose their regenerative capacity as senescent CPCs induce senescence in other healthy CPCs through paracrine mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C69 are supported by citation (Lewis-McDougall et al. 2019). This demonstrates paracrine senescence in a specific stem cell population, contributing to age-related decline in cardiac regeneration. The evidence shows propagation of senescence within progenitor cell populations.

results.result: Senescent dermal fibroblasts express atypical levels of MHC molecule HLA-E (induced by SASP cytokines and regulated by p38MAPK), which interacts with the inhibitory receptor NKG2A on NK and CD8+ T cells, allowing senescent cells to evade immune clearance.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C71 are supported by citation (Pereira et al. 2019) and inference about HLA-E function. This provides a specific mechanism for immune evasion by senescent cells, which helps explain their accumulation with age. The evidence demonstrates a molecular mechanism of immunosurveillance escape.

results.result: Overexpression of oncogenic Ras in human fibroblasts results in upregulation of p53, p16INK4a, pRB, and permanent cell cycle arrest (oncogene-induced senescence). This can be bypassed by inactivation of p53 and p16INK4a or co-expression of other oncogenes like c-MYC, E1A, or DRIL1.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C74 are supported by citation (Serrano et al. 1997). This establishes the molecular basis of oncogene-induced senescence and demonstrates that it functions as a tumor suppressor mechanism that can be overcome. The evidence is from a landmark study in the field.

results.result: BRAF promotes oncogene-induced senescence by inducing p16INK4a expression in a process that requires co-expression of IGFBP7.
results.evaluation: Claim C75 is supported by citation (Wajapeyee et al. 2008). This identifies another oncogene that induces senescence and reveals a requirement for IGFBP7, adding to understanding of OIS mechanisms.

results.result: Loss of PTEN induces a senescence response through activation of p53 (via mTOR and ARF-mediated inhibition of MDM2) and p16INK4a (via upregulation of transcription factor Ets2). Unlike OIS, PTEN loss-induced senescence occurs without DNA damage response but can be bypassed by p53 inactivation.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C80 are supported by citations (Chen et al. 2005, Ohtani et al. 2001). This demonstrates that tumor suppressor loss can also induce senescence through distinct mechanisms from oncogene activation. The evidence reveals mechanistic diversity in senescence induction.

results.result: Release of IL-1α by senescent cells spreads senescence to normal and tumor cells, while inhibition of IL-1α and IL-6 promotes oncogene-induced senescence evasion.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C82 are supported by citations (Di Mitri and Alimonti 2016, Kuilman et al. 2008). This demonstrates that SASP factors can both reinforce and propagate senescence, and that blocking these factors allows senescence escape. The evidence shows the dual role of SASP in tumor suppression.

results.result: Some SASP factors from tumor cells (TGF-β, VEGF, CCL2, CCL20) induce senescence in normal cells. The immune response can limit tumourigenesis by releasing factors (IFN-γ, TNF-α, TGF-β) that induce senescence in tumor cells, creating a positive feedback loop.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C84 are supported by citations (Acosta et al. 2013, Braumüller et al. 2013, Calcinotto et al. 2019, Reimann et al. 2010). This demonstrates bidirectional interactions between senescent cells and the immune system in the tumor microenvironment. The evidence shows complex paracrine signaling networks.

results.result: The SASP can have immunosuppressive properties by attracting myeloid-derived suppressor cells that block other immune effector populations and inhibit the senescence response by releasing IL-1 receptor antagonist in the tumor microenvironment.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C86 are supported by citation (Di Mitri et al. 2014). This demonstrates that the SASP can also suppress immune responses, adding complexity to understanding of senescence in cancer. The evidence shows context-dependent immune modulation.

results.result: The SASP of senescent tumor cells can promote tumor progression by driving vascularization and invasiveness through secretion of VEGF, matrix metalloproteinases, Gro-α, basic fibroblast growth factor, and PAI-1. IL-6 and IL-8 secretion can promote both tumourigenesis and tumor suppression in different contexts.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C89 are supported by citations (Coppé et al. 2006, Coppé et al. 2010, Rodier and Campisi 2011). This demonstrates the pro-tumorigenic potential of the SASP, contrasting with its tumor suppressive role. The evidence establishes the context-dependent effects of SASP factors.

results.result: Telomerase-deficient zebrafish exhibit senescence accumulation similar to human aging and display increased systemic chronic inflammation that potentiates cancer incidence and invasiveness. Pre-cancer lesions develop into cancer at twice the rate if neighboring tissues are senescent.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C91 are supported by citation (Lex et al. 2020) and inference from the study context. This provides in vivo evidence that persistent senescence and chronic inflammation promote cancer progression. The zebrafish model demonstrates the pro-tumorigenic effects of senescence accumulation.

results.result: Chemotherapy drugs or ionizing radiation induce therapy-induced senescence (TIS) in cancer cells through DNA damage response mechanisms. Several TIS drugs are used clinically including Palbociclib (the most relevant CDK4/6 inhibitor), Doxorubicin, Bleomycin, Docetaxel, Cyclophosphamide, Etoposide, Vincristine, and Cisplatin.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C95 are supported by citations (Calcinotto et al. 2019, Ewald et al. 2010). This establishes the clinical application of senescence induction as a cancer therapy. The evidence demonstrates the therapeutic relevance of senescence biology.

results.result: Accumulation of senescent cells after therapy-induced senescence promotes tumor relapse with increased malignancy. Some senescent tumor cells can escape cell cycle blockade and acquire stemness properties with aggressive growth potential. Current therapeutic strategies use a double approach: initial pro-senescent step followed by anti-senescent phase.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C98 are supported by citations (Marcoux et al. 2013, Ness et al. 2015, Milanovic et al. 2018, Calcinotto et al. 2019). This reveals important limitations and complications of senescence-based cancer therapy. The evidence demonstrates the need for combination approaches to prevent adverse outcomes.

results.result: Senescent cells have been found during development in mouse and human embryos, as well as in naked mole rats, birds, amphibians, and fish embryos and/or larvae.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C103 are supported by multiple citations (Chuprin et al. 2013, Muñoz-Espín et al. 2013, Storer et al. 2013, Zhao et al. 2018, Gibaja et al. 2019, Nacher et al. 2006, Davaapil et al. 2017, Villiard et al. 2017, Da Silva-Álvarez et al. 2020). This establishes that senescence is a conserved developmental phenomenon across vertebrates. The evidence demonstrates the evolutionary conservation and physiological role of developmental senescence.

results.result: Senescent cells in developing embryonic structures exhibit SA-β-gal activity and p21CIP1 upregulation, but lack p53, p16INK4a, and DNA damage response. Genetic disruption of p21CIP1 or senolytic treatment causes loss of senescence and patterning abnormalities that are transiently observed and eventually compensated by apoptosis. This suggests senescent cells are intrinsic to development but not essential, and developmental senescence is a highly organized, programmed process with precise spatiotemporal patterns.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C108 are supported by citations (Muñoz-Espín et al. 2013, Davaapil et al. 2017, Gibaja et al. 2019, Storer et al. 2013) and inference from developmental studies. This characterizes developmental senescence as distinct from stress-induced senescence and demonstrates its role in tissue patterning. The evidence shows that developmental senescence has unique features and functions.

results.result: A role of senescence in wound healing and tissue repair has been described in the liver, skin, heart, and lung. Senescent cells are closely associated with the levels of fibrotic tissue generated upon wound resolution, which affects the repair outcome.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C113 are supported by citations (Krizhanovsky et al. 2008, Demaria et al. 2014, Jun and Lau 2010, Meyer et al. 2016, Zhu et al. 2013, Schafer et al. 2017, Baker et al. 2016, Yun 2018). This establishes the role of senescence in tissue repair across multiple organs. The evidence demonstrates that senescence modulates fibrosis during wound healing.

results.result: In the skin, CCN1 elicits a senescence response in fibroblasts by triggering p53 and p16INK4a via ERK and p38MAPK pathways. This response controls fibroblast proliferation and ECM deposition, limiting fibrotic scar and contributing to healing. Defects in CCN1 lead to fibrosis exacerbation.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C116 are supported by citation (Jun and Lau 2010) and inference about CCN1 function. This provides a specific molecular mechanism for senescence-mediated control of fibrosis during wound healing. The evidence demonstrates the anti-fibrotic role of senescence in skin repair.

results.result: Transient accumulation of senescent fibroblasts and endothelial cells at wound sites induces myofibroblast differentiation through PDGF-AA secretion. Elimination of p16+ cells results in delayed wound healing and increased fibrosis. Topical PDGF-AA administration reverts the delay in wound closure while maintaining fibrotic tissue levels, suggesting additional SASP factors (likely MMPs) are involved.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C119 are supported by citation (Demaria et al. 2014) and experimental results with inference about MMPs. This demonstrates the beneficial role of transient senescence in wound healing and identifies specific SASP factors involved. The evidence uses genetic ablation and rescue experiments to establish causality.

results.result: In a mouse model of chronic liver damage, CCl4 administration induces fibrotic scarring and senescence in hepatic stellate cells via a CCN1/p53/p16INK4a pathway. Senescent HSCs facilitate fibrotic resolution through MMP secretion and recruit NK cells for their own elimination. p53;INK4A/ARF null mice display decreased senescent HSCs and extensive cirrhosis upon CCl4 treatment.
results.evaluation: Claims C120-C123 are supported by citation (Krizhanovsky et al. 2008). This demonstrates the beneficial role of senescence in liver repair through fibrosis resolution and immune-mediated clearance. The genetic loss-of-function experiments provide strong causal evidence.

results.result: In ischemic retinopathy, the SASP of senescent endothelial cells stimulates neutrophil recruitment and neutrophil extracellular trap extrusion, which removes dysfunctional senescent endothelial cells and facilitates vascular pruning and repair.
results.evaluation: Claim C124 is supported by citation (Binet et al. 2020). This demonstrates a specific mechanism of immune-mediated senescent cell clearance during vascular repair. The evidence shows the beneficial role of transient senescence in retinal vascular remodeling.

results.result: In mouse models of cardiac hypertrophy and heart infarction, cardiac myofibroblasts enter CCN1-dependent senescence, reducing short-term fibrosis and improving heart function. However, after cardiac ischaemia-reperfusion injury, long-term oxidative stress-induced senescence in cardiomyocytes and interstitial cells promotes fibrosis and pro-inflammatory SASP, impairing heart function.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C126 are supported by citations (Meyer et al. 2016, Zhu et al. 2013, Dookun et al. 2020). This demonstrates the time-dependent effects of senescence in cardiac injury: beneficial when transient, detrimental when persistent. The evidence clearly shows the importance of temporal dynamics.

results.result: In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, senescent epithelial cells and fibroblasts accumulate continuously over time, inducing myofibroblast differentiation and exacerbating the fibrotic response. Elimination of senescent cells improves the disease condition.
results.evaluation: Claims C127-C128 are supported by citation (Schafer et al. 2017). This demonstrates the detrimental role of persistent senescence in chronic fibrotic disease. The evidence shows that senescent cell elimination is therapeutic in this context.

results.result: Timely and coordinated activation of senescent cells controls the early fibrotic response and is beneficial for wound repair. However, in the absence of proper clearance, persistent senescent cells accumulate and have a negative impact on tissue repair.
results.evaluation: Claims C129-C130 are inferred from collective evidence on wound healing with reference to Figure 2. This synthesizes the key principle that emerges from wound healing studies: transient senescence is beneficial, persistent senescence is detrimental. The inference is well-supported by the preceding evidence.

results.result: A recurrent turnover of senescence occurs during limb regeneration in the salamander. Senescent cells are transiently induced near the amputation plane throughout regeneration and subsequently cleared by a macrophage-dependent immunosurveillance mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C131-C132 are supported by citation (Yun et al. 2015). This is the first demonstration of senescence during regeneration in a highly regenerative vertebrate. The evidence establishes a link between senescence and regeneration.

results.result: A transient burst of SA-β-gal+ cardiac fibroblasts was reported in zebrafish and neonatal mouse hearts after injury. Telomerase-deficient zebrafish display aberrant accumulation of senescent cells and fail to regenerate their hearts.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C134 are supported by citations (Sarig et al. 2019, Bednarek et al. 2015). This demonstrates that transient senescence occurs during cardiac regeneration, and aberrant accumulation impairs regeneration. The evidence suggests senescence dynamics are important for regenerative outcomes.

results.result: A transient accumulation of senescent cells occurs after zebrafish caudal fin amputation. Tissue regeneration is impaired by removal of senescent cells with a senolytic drug.
results.evaluation: Claims C135-C136 are supported by citations (Da Silva‐Álvarez et al. 2019, Zhu et al. 2015). This provides direct evidence that senescent cells are required for regeneration in zebrafish. The pharmacological depletion experiment demonstrates causality.

results.result: In a mouse model of chronic inflammatory myopathy, senescence of fibro-adipogenic progenitors in response to exercise-induced muscle damage is necessary to promote functional recovery and muscle regeneration.
results.evaluation: Claim C137 is supported by citation (Saito et al. 2020). This demonstrates a beneficial role of senescence in muscle regeneration through modulation of the inflammatory environment. The evidence shows senescence can promote regeneration in specific contexts.

results.result: The expression of p53 is upregulated in the rat soleus muscle after spinal cord injury.
results.evaluation: Claim C138 is supported by citation (Graham et al. 2020), but the authors note this study lacks key senescence biomarkers like SA-β-gal and p21CIP1. Without comprehensive characterization, it is uncertain whether this represents true senescence or another form of p53 activation. Additional markers would be needed to confirm senescence.

results.result: In a mouse model of biliary injury, TGF-β secretion-mediated paracrine senescence of cholangiocytes and hepatocytes has deleterious repercussions in the surrounding microenvironment and impairs liver regeneration. Inhibition of TGF-β signaling disrupts the continuous propagation of senescence, reduces collagen deposition, and restores liver function.
results.evaluation: Claims C139-C140 are supported by citation (Ferreira-Gonzalez et al. 2018). This demonstrates the detrimental role of persistent paracrine senescence in liver regeneration and shows that blocking senescence propagation is therapeutic. The evidence clearly demonstrates the negative impact of chronic senescence.

results.result: After spinal cord injury, regenerating zebrafish exhibit transient accumulation of senescent cells at the lesion periphery that are cleared, while injured mice show persistent accumulation without elimination. Targeting senescent cells in the mouse spinal cord to prevent their accumulation results in improved motor, sensory, and bladder functions, with beneficial effects on myelin preservation, axonal growth, fibrotic resolution, inflammation, and reduced secretion of pro-fibrotic and pro-inflammatory factors.
results.evaluation: Claims C141-C144 are stated as findings from the authors' own study (Paramos-de-Carvalho et al. 2021). This demonstrates that the key difference between regenerating and non-regenerating spinal cord injury is the temporal dynamics of senescence. The evidence provides strong support for the central thesis that transient senescence is beneficial while persistent senescence is detrimental.

results.result: In vitro, expression of the four Yamanaka factors (OSKM) activates senescence markers in targeting cells. The iPS cell generation efficiency is approximately 0.02%, and silencing of senescence-associated genes like p53, CIP1, and INK4a increases iPS cell generation rate from mouse and human fibroblasts.
results.evaluation: Claims C145-C147 are supported by citations (Banito et al. 2009, Takahashi et al. 2007, Takahashi and Yamanaka 2006, Hong et al. 2009, Li et al. 2009). This demonstrates that senescence acts as a barrier to in vitro reprogramming. The evidence shows that overcoming senescence improves reprogramming efficiency.

results.result: In i4F wild-type mice, SA-β-gal and NANOG are co-expressed, but this is lost without INK4a/ARF. In mouse models of lung and muscle damage where senescence is induced, reprogramming efficiency of i4F mice is increased. Reprogramming efficiency is enhanced by conditions that elicit senescence (Palbociclib, irradiation, aging) and decreased by p16INK4a deletion or ABT-263 treatment. This senescence-induced favorable environment is mediated by IL-6 secretion that activates JAK/STAT target PIM1 to promote cellular plasticity.
results.evaluation: Claims C148-C153 are supported by citations (Mosteiro et al. 2016, Chiche et al. 2017). This demonstrates that senescence promotes in vivo reprogramming, opposite to its effect in vitro. The evidence identifies IL-6/JAK/STAT/PIM1 as the mechanistic pathway. This is a major conceptual advance showing context-dependent effects of senescence.

results.result: Ras-mediated oncogene-induced senescence in skin and liver induces expression of stemness markers (CD34, Lgr6, Nestin) in senescent keratinocytes in a SASP-dependent manner that is abolished by NF-κB inhibition. However, expression of stemness markers is overcome by senescence features upon longer (6 days) exposure to the OIS-driven SASP, proposed as a cell-intrinsic anti-tumorigenic response.
results.evaluation: Claims C154-C156 are supported by citation (Ritschka et al. 2017) and experimental results with interpretation. This demonstrates that senescence can transiently induce stemness before being overcome by senescence features. The evidence shows time-dependent effects of the SASP on cellular plasticity.

results.result: Senescent liver sinusoid endothelial cells have important structural and functional roles in the aging organism and cannot be replaced after removal. Acute elimination of these cells promotes liver and perivascular tissue fibrosis and health deterioration.
results.evaluation: Claims C157-C158 are supported by citation (Grosse et al. 2020). This demonstrates that not all senescent cells are detrimental and some have important physiological functions. The evidence provides an important caveat to senolytic approaches.

results.result: Transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulation of pro-survival genes in senescent cells, including the anti-apoptotic PI3K/AKT pathway and BCL-2 family proteins. Senolytic agents such as Dasatinib, Quercetin, and Navitoclax are being tested in clinical trials for senescence/age-associated disorders and cancer.
results.evaluation: Claims C159-C160 are supported by citations (Zhu et al. 2015, Paez-Ribes et al. 2019). This establishes the molecular basis for senolytic drug development and the clinical translation of senescence biology. The evidence demonstrates the therapeutic potential of targeting senescent cells.

results.result: In vitro studies show NK and CD4+ T cell sensitization towards senescent cells upon administration of anti-DPP4 and anti-Vimentin antibodies. CAR T cells targeting urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR), broadly expressed during senescence, efficiently eliminate senescent cells in different in vitro and in vivo contexts.
results.evaluation: Claims C161-C163 are supported by citations (Frescas et al. 2017, Kim et al. 2017, Amor et al. 2020) and reference to Figure 1. This demonstrates immune-based approaches to target senescent cells. The CAR T cell approach is particularly promising as it provides specificity and potency.

results.result: CD9 is upregulated in endothelial cells and associated with atherosclerotic plaque formation. CD9 regulates cellular senescence through a PI3K-AKT-mTOR-p53 signaling pathway, and its expression increases in arterial tissues with age, contributing to atherosclerosis pathogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C164-C166 are supported by citation (Cho et al. 2020). This identifies CD9 as a potential therapeutic target for vascular aging and demonstrates a specific signaling pathway. The evidence shows the relevance of senescence to cardiovascular disease.

results.result: A combination of 5‐Azacytydine and Resveratrol reverses the senescent phenotype of adipose stem cells through modulation of mitochondrial dynamics and autophagy. Upon treatment, cells exhibit increased proliferation rate, decreased SA-β-gal activity, and lower ROS accumulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C167-C168 are supported by citation (Kornicka et al. 2019). This demonstrates that senescence can be reversed through pharmacological intervention. The evidence supports the concept of 'senoreverters' as an alternative to senolytics.

results.result: Replicative senescent retinal pigment epithelial cells co-cultured with embryonic stem cells display increased proliferative capacity, re-entering S and G2/M cycle phases, with downregulation of senescence biomarkers.
results.evaluation: Claim C169 is supported by citation (Wang et al. 2020). This demonstrates that senescence can be reversed through paracrine signals from stem cells. The evidence supports the concept of senescence reversal.

results.result: PDK1 inhibition suppresses NF-κB and mTOR signaling and abolishes senescence hallmarks in senescent human dermal fibroblasts, restoring their quiescent state.
results.evaluation: Claim C170 is supported by citation (An et al. 2020). This identifies a specific molecular target for senescence reversal and demonstrates restoration of quiescence. The evidence provides a mechanistic approach to senescence reversal.

results.result: The senescence program entails deep epigenetic alterations that permit tight regulation of transcriptional activities essential to its timely execution. This epigenetic network is orchestrated by activator protein 1 (AP-1), which 'imprints' the senescence enhancer landscape that drives the transcriptional program and determines senescent cell fate.
results.evaluation: Claims C171-C172 are supported by citation (Martínez-Zamudio et al. 2020). This identifies AP-1 as a master regulator of the senescence epigenetic program. The evidence demonstrates the importance of epigenetic regulation in senescence.

results.result: The balance between senescence and apoptosis upon genotoxic stress is regulated by HMGB1 proteins. A crosstalk between the telomere shortening/p53 and AKT/FoxO signaling pathways regulates an apoptosis-to-senescence switch during aging.
results.evaluation: Claims C173-C174 are supported by citations (Lee et al. 2019, El Maï et al. 2020). This addresses the important question of what determines whether cells undergo senescence versus apoptosis. The evidence identifies specific regulatory mechanisms.

results.result: Organs of regenerating animals such as zebrafish often display senescence features during their developmental stages, suggesting a link between regeneration and recapitulation of developmental senescence.
results.evaluation: Claim C175 is supported by citation (Da Silva-Álvarez et al. 2020). This suggests that regeneration may recapitulate developmental programs including senescence. The evidence provides a conceptual link between development and regeneration.

results.result: Two distinct populations of p16INK4a+ and p21CIP1+ senescent cells respectively promote and impair the regenerative capacity of the mouse liver.
results.evaluation: Claim C176 is supported by citation (Ritschka et al. 2020). This demonstrates that different senescent cell populations can have opposite effects on regeneration. The evidence shows the complexity of senescence heterogeneity.

results.result: The beneficial roles of senescence all share a transient profile, while the deleterious functions of senescent cells are associated with their lingering persistence and chronic exposure to their SASP.
results.evaluation: Claims C177-C178 are inferred from collective evidence with reference to Figure 2 and citation (Rhinn et al. 2019). This synthesizes the central thesis of the review: time is the key factor determining whether senescence is beneficial or detrimental. The inference is well-supported by the extensive evidence presented throughout the manuscript.
